'''Sergey Bobkov''' (Russian: Сергей Германович Бобков; born 15 March 1961) is a Russian mathematician. Currently Bobkov is a professor at the University of Minnesota, Twin Cities.

He was born in [[Vorkuta]] ([[Komi Republic|Komi Republic, Russia]]) and graduated from the Department of Mathematics and Mechanics in [[Leningrad State University]]. In 1988 he earned PhD in Mathematics and Physics (under direction of Vladimir N. Sudakov, [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]])  and in 1997 earned his Doctor of Science. During 1998–2000 Bobkov held positions at [[Syktyvkar State University]], Russia.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.umn.edu/~bobkov/documents/CV_S.G.Bobkov_Nov2013_web.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae: Sergey G. Bobkov |date=November 2013 |publisher=University of Minnesota School of Mathematics|accessdate=27 May 2014}}</ref> From 1995 to 1996 he was an [[Alexander von Humboldt Fellow]] at [[Bielefeld University]], Germany. He spent the summers of 2001 and 2002 as an EPSRC Fellow at [[Imperial College London]], UK.<ref name="berkeley">{{cite web|url=http://simons.berkeley.edu/people/sergey-bobkov|title=Sergey Bobkov |work=Current long-term visitors |publisher=Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing|accessdate=2014-05-05}}</ref>  Bobkov was awarded a Simons Fellowship (2012) and [[Humboldt Prize|Humboldt Research Award]] (2014).<ref name="humboldt-foundation">{{cite web|url=http://www.humboldt-foundation.de/pls/web/pub_laudatio.main?p_lang=en&p_fgb=2A|title=Awardees: Mathematics |work=Humboldt Network |publisher=Alexander von Humboldt-Stiftung/Foundation |accessdate=2014-05-05}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2012 Simons Fellows Awardees: Mathematics|url=http://www.simonsfoundation.org/funding/2012-simons-fellows-awardees-mathematics/|publisher=Simons Foundation|accessdate=27 May 2014}}</ref> 

Bobkov is known for research in mathematics on the border of [[probability theory]], [[Analysis (mathematics)|analysis]], [[convex geometry]] and [[information theory]]. He has achieved important results about [[isoperimetric problems]], [[concentration of measure]] and other high-dimensional phenomena.

[[Bobkov's inequality]] is named after him.
